title: Can Claude Code actually help me create football animations and 3D models for my game?
author: Alone-Influence-3572
selftext:
Hey  
I’m currently developing a football game, and I’ve started running into a pretty frustrating problem: finding good assets.  
I’ve already explored most of the free or affordable animation resources available online. It’s pretty much the same story with 3D player models. Eventually, you keep coming across the same animations and models, with very limited customization options.  
So I’ve been wondering whether **Claude Code could help me take things further.**  
For example:  
Could it help create football animations based on video references?  
Can it generate Blender scripts or tools to make creating and modifying 3D models easier?  
Could it automate parts of the rigging, animation, or character integration process in a game engine?  
Could I use it to build my own animation production tools instead of constantly relying on assets found online?  
I’m not necessarily expecting Claude to generate a complete 3D player or fully finished animation by itself. I’m more interested in using its coding capabilities to improve and automate parts of the development pipeline.  
I’d also love some advice from people who regularly use Claude Code.  
**How do you manage your usage to avoid burning through your limits and tokens too quickly?**  
Any best practices? Prompt organization, context files, breaking tasks into smaller pieces, code management, etc.  
I’d especially appreciate feedback from indie game developers, Blender users, and people working with 3D animation.  
Thanks!

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
gonna take u alot of wizardry and may still be halfbaked , most people tend to stick with 2d and effect , if not there are a few OS tools from nvidia and meta you can try , also things like cascadeur . What you want is to mask and isolate the movement in a real video then simulate it in something like cascadeur or another similar tool. 

Alternatively people have been using high quality image to video models with first frame last frame, generate then render each as an action and use something like after effect to stitch together ( read it and saw an game on here that did so ) 

But clean 3d thing and animations are a massive headache for us all unless u know blender, the issue is relaying what u want and what tools to use in blender , sometimes i even feed it youtube transcripts on a specific technique .  

and to avoid burning tokens u gotta research that on your own, it boils down to limiting mcps , deciding which model and effort level gets results , being descriptive enough to not ask the same thing 4 times , and having a x10 plan. Also gpt gives more tokens in a plan but in my time using it they produce poor quality for coding , you may have better luck with blender . 

and last thing once shit get good make skills so the agent knows the work flow , also make plugins for blender...example you wouldnt need to make a jersey every time instead u make a jersey maker that takes the top , bottom and change colors , numbers etc.
